name: Dumbbell Scaption
summary: A shoulder isolation exercise where dumbbells are raised in the scapular plane, roughly thirty to forty-five degrees forward of the torso, to strengthen the deltoids with minimal subacromial impingement.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Slightly bend your elbows and rotate your hands so your thumbs point slightly upward or toward each other in a neutral to semi-neutral grip.
steps: Raise both arms along the scapular plane, approximately 30 to 45 degrees forward from purely sideways.
Continue raising until your hands reach shoulder height, maintaining the slight elbow bend and leading slightly with the thumbs.
Pause briefly at the top while maintaining control without shrugging excessively.
Lower the dumbbells smoothly along the same diagonal path back to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells; inhale smoothly as you lower them.
cues: Reach out into a wide V.
Lead with the thumbs slightly up.
Keep shoulders down away from ears.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core, stay upright, and reduce the weight so the shoulders perform all the work.

common_faults.fault: Raising arms purely to the side in the frontal plane.
common_faults.correction: Angling the arms 30 to 45 degrees forward aligns movement with the shoulder blade and avoids joint pinch.
Focus on reaching the dumbbells outward toward the walls rather than pulling upward with the upper traps.

precautions: Do not internally rotate the shoulders (thumbs pointing down) during the raise to avoid subacromial impingement.
